solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Elitist completely accepts women grow ever faster

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the elitist's word takes the women's letter inside it

parts.note: a snob looks down on others, an elitist
all means wholly or completely

explanation.surface: A thorough snob lets women in, and things then accelerate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grow ever faster' is a verb phrase; the image is a rolling ball gathering snow.
explanation.definitionFit: To snowball is to gather momentum like a rolling ball of snow, growing and speeding up.

clue.text: Hardly ever cause permanent damage to church

parts.note: to scar is to leave a lasting mark
CE is Church of England

explanation.surface: Something that seldom permanently damages a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The adverb sense, as in 'scarce had he arrived', is literary.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb this is a literary form of scarcely, meaning only just or seldom.

clue.text: Turning model truck away from its top and carrying on

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the shortened vehicle holds the other piece
away from its top means the first letter of the truck word is lost

parts.note: a lorry is the British word for a truck
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A toy truck spun round, top removed, carries on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' looks like it acts on the truck, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system whose planets revolve.

clue.text: A single male long entertained by bishop and peer mostly

indicators.note: being entertained by someone puts you in their company, so the yearning word goes inside

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the peer's word is dropped

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
to long for is to ache for

explanation.surface: An unmarried man pining while hosted by a bishop and a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is an unmarried man, hence one who is single.

clue.text: Instrument that's not musically loud?

indicators.note: not here means without, so a letter is removed from the instrument

parts.note: a flute is a woodwind instrument
f stands for forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A query about a quiet instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes F (forte) from FLUTE. The whole clue also describes the soft-toned plucked instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The lute is a gentle plucked string instrument of the Renaissance, never a loud one.

clue.text: Some bang up politicians over dispute

indicators.note: over signals the run of letters is turned back to front
some of the words means only part of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: Banging up politicians is something to argue about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes NGUPPO from 'bang up politicians'; 'over' turns it round. OPPUGN is a rare formal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppugn is a formal, rather old word for calling into question or contesting.

clue.text: Quite trivial, capturing rook

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner, so the chess piece goes inside

parts.note: petty means trivial
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A trifling chess move that takes a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts R inside PETTY.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means fairly or moderately, as in 'fairly good'.

clue.text: Barbarians, emotional but lacking any aspiration, ousted in election?

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathed h sound, so every h is dropped

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders
heated means emotional or passionate

explanation.surface: Uncouth, passionate politicians with no ambition lose their places at the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking any aspiration' drops both H's (the breathed sound) from HUNS HEATED.
explanation.definitionFit: An MP who loses a seat at the polls has been removed from office.

clue.text: Prepared sea-snail, to render not just in the mouth

definitions.text: to render not just in the mouth

indicators.note: food that is prepared is chopped and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cooked sea snail to be served up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' rearranges SEASNAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To nasalise a sound is to make it through the nose as well as the mouth.

clue.text: A communist reduced business centre's barbarity

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the word for a communist goes

parts.note: a Trot is a Trotskyist, a type of communist
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A cut-down communist complains about the cruelty of the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London is Britain's financial centre. 'reduced' cuts TROT to TRO.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is an act of extreme cruelty, a synonym of barbarity.

clue.text: Thesis wasted in bank jobs etc

indicators.note: wasted suggests something destroyed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wasted thesis is found among records of robberies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' rearranges THESIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Heists are robberies, with bank raids the classic examples.

clue.text: Want leader of party openly rejecting the Left?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
rejecting means throwing out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: overtly means openly
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A party leader openly rejecting the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' takes L out of OVERTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Want, as a noun, means lack of necessities, i.e. destitution.

clue.text: Fellow in fix with travel restriction

indicators.note: in places the fellow's letter inside the following pieces

parts.note: to cure is to fix or remedy

explanation.surface: A man in a tight spot because he cannot move about freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts F inside CURE+W.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is an order keeping people indoors at certain hours, restricting movement.

clue.text: Step flat out to intercept 31

indicators.note: to intercept is to get in the way, so the scrambled letters go into the middle of the other word

parts.note: the 31 across answer is an idiot, so a fool

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A step taken flat out to cut off an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat out' looks like a phrase meaning at full speed; here 'out' rearranges the letters of 'flat' alone. 31 is the idiot across.
explanation.definitionFit: A footfall is the sound or act of a single step.

clue.text: Strongly supporting stem

definitions.meaning: loyal and committed, as a firm ally is
to stop the flow of something, as of blood from a wound

explanation.surface: Firm backing for a plant's stalk.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means loyal; as a verb, a variant of stanch, to stop a flow.

clue.text: Decrepit old jet's pushed around

indicators.note: decrepit means worn out and falling apart, signalling letters rearranged

parts.note: the word jets, with its s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A worn-out old aircraft has been shoved about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decrepit' rearranges OLD JETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be jostled is to be bumped and shoved, as in a crowd.

clue.text: Animal cries from converted stables

definitions.meaning: the plaintive calls of cats or gulls
a row of former stables made into homes, a British term for such a street

explanation.surface: Animal noises coming from a converted stable block.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this also names a back street of stables turned into houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means cat or gull calls, and also stables built round a yard, now often homes.

clue.text: Shallow person: there's an improvement in me, mostly after 3

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the cross-referenced letter

parts.note: 3 down is a single male, abbreviated B as in a degree or listing

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: said as I'm better

explanation.surface: A shallow person claims to be getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: B abbreviates the 3 down answer (a single man); 'there's an improvement in me' is I'M BETTER, cut by 'mostly' to IMBETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bimbette is a slangy term for a vacuous young woman, a superficial person.

clue.text: Special salad plant engaging tooth

parts.note: rocket is a peppery salad leaf

explanation.surface: A special salad leaf caught in the teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocket is the British name for arugula.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprocket is a projection on a wheel that meshes with a chain's links.

clue.text: Routines given away by French monk keeping reverence up?

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the monk's word holds the other piece

parts.note: frere is French for brother, a monk

indicators.note: up in a down clue signals reading backwards

parts.note: awe is reverence

explanation.surface: A French monk handing out his devotions while remaining reverent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Routines' suggests a monk's daily devotions, but means computer programs.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeware is software distributed without charge; 'routines' is a programming sense.

clue.text: Fringe elements among insurgents play childish game

indicators.note: the fringe of a word is its edge, so the first and last letters of each word are used

explanation.surface: Fringe groups among the rebels behave like children playing.
explanation.walkthrough: I spy is a guessing game played by children.
explanation.definitionFit: I spy is a guessing game in which children name things by their first letter.

clue.text: Thickened milk containing mixed ingredients for taste?

definitions.text: Thickened milk containing mixed ingredients for taste?

indicators.note: containing means the milk word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: curd is milk thickened by curdling

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred into a new order
ingredients are only some of a dish's parts, so just part of the word taste is used

explanation.surface: A recipe note: milk thickened with flavourings added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredients for' keeps TAS of 'taste' and 'mixed' rearranges it to STA. The whole clue also describes the sweet sauce, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This dessert sauce is milk thickened with egg or cornflour and sweetened for flavour.

clue.text: Possible explanation for Sue's bad treatment?

indicators.note: a possible explanation tells how a thing came about, so the solver gives wordplay that would produce the next word

parts.note: read as wordplay, the letters of 'use' arranged badly give this name

explanation.surface: Someone guessing why Sue was mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'ill' can signal a jumble, so ILL USE would be wordplay producing SUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone cruelly is to mistreat them; the hyphenated noun names that abuse.

clue.text: For instance, Zimbabwe is bordered by this decorative strip

indicators.note: bordered points to the edges, so first and last letters of each word are used

explanation.surface: Using a country as an example of land with a decorative edging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bordered' takes the outside letters of 'For', 'instance' and 'Zimbabwe': FR, IE, ZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is an ornamental horizontal band along a wall.

clue.text: Carried off wayward youth as usual

parts.note: to carry off a prize is to win it
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a rebellious 1950s British youth

explanation.surface: A delinquent youth took the prize as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonted is an old word for habitual or customary.

clue.text: Wellington doesn't need one to secure account in Merseyside port

definitions.text: Wellington doesn't need one to secure

indicators.note: in places the account abbreviation inside the port's name

parts.note: Bootle is a dock town beside Liverpool on Merseyside

explanation.surface: The Duke of Wellington securing an account in a Liverpool-area port.
explanation.walkthrough: A wellington is a rubber boot pulled on without fastening; Bootle is a port town in Merseyside, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A lace ties a shoe on, but a wellington boot simply slips on, so needs none.

clue.text: River trap to provide odd fish?

parts.note: a weir is a dam across a river, also used as a fish trap
to do can mean to provide, as in doing lunch

explanation.surface: A river fish trap set up to catch a strange fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd fish' is slang for a strange person, not a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd fish is an eccentric person, the same as a strange oddball.

clue.text: After switching sections, approve floor

indicators.note: the front part of the word is moved behind the rest

parts.note: to okay is to approve

explanation.surface: A floor plan approved after rearranging sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching sections' moves the O of OKAY to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayo is a knockout, and to kayo someone is to knock them to the floor.

clue.text: Accept a brew container from an Irish speaker?

indicators.note: in a stereotyped Irish accent the word tea is said 'tay', so the container is heard differently

parts.note: a teacup holds a brew of tea

explanation.surface: Taking a mug of tea offered by someone from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The stage-Irish 'tay' for tea turns TEACUP into the sound of TAKE UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up an offer is to accept it.

clue.text: An inclination to stuff favourite bird

indicators.note: to stuff is to fill, so the favourite's word is filled with the other letters

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
an gives the letter A
rake is the slope or inclination of a stage or mast

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to stuff a favourite bird, like a taxidermist.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small long-tailed parrot, so a kind of bird.

clue.text: Medium supposedly taking one in as a first option?

indicators.note: taking in means accommodating, so the one is placed within the medium's word

parts.note: ether was once supposed to be the medium carrying light through space
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A psychic medium taking someone in as the preferred choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic, but it is the ether once thought to fill space. 'taking ... in' puts I inside ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'X or Y' choices the word introduces the first alternative of two.

clue.text: A single male imprisoned by evil idiot

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held inside, so the evil word surrounds the others

parts.note: bad means evil
a single thing is one
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A single man locked up by a wicked fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonehead is a stupid person, a dimwit.
